chunks: And the hadith narrated by Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa and Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Marwak ibn 'Ubayd from Nashit ibn Salih from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (AS) — he said:
"It is sufficient for urine to wash it with its equivalent."

This is firstly a mursal hadith, because Nashit said 'from some of our companions.' Moreover, the first hadith had been narrated as musnad with content that contradicts what this hadith contains. It is also possible that the narrator made an error (wahm) in transmitting it. And even if it were sound and valid, it would be possible that by his saying 'with its equivalent' he meant the equivalent of what comes out as urine — which is more than twice what remains on the tip of the glans. And what reveals this interpretation [continues in the following section]...

key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: mursal — hadith whose chain of narrators contains a missing link
key_terms.مُسْنَداً: musnad — hadith with a fully connected chain of narrators
key_terms.وَهِمَ: to err in narration; the narrator's false impression (wahm)

ai.seo_question: What is Sheikh al-Tusi's critique of the hadith that urine is purified by washing with its equivalent amount of water in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This passage from Tahdhib al-Ahkam quotes a hadith from Imam Abu 'Abdillah (AS) that it is sufficient to wash urine with an equal amount of water, then subjects it to a three-pronged critique by Sheikh al-Tusi: (1) the hadith is mursal because the intermediate narrator is anonymous; (2) it contradicts an earlier musnad hadith; (3) even if sound, 'with its equivalent' may be re-interpreted as the total volume of urine passed — which exceeds twice what remains on the tip of the glans.
